I am a resident in Ward 4 and a constituent of your council in the City of Toronto. I am writing to draw your attention to the issue of water waste in our ward. I have observed an increase in overwatering of lawns during the day, which is a significant concern given our limited water resources.

The City of Toronto currently suggests that individuals and businesses water their lawns no more than once per week during off-peak hours (between 11 p.m. and 8 a.m.), but this is merely a recommendation rather than an enforceable bylaw (City of Toronto, 2020a). Additionally, the City can issue an 'Outdoor Water Use Advisory' when water supplies are low, but this does not carry the same legal weight as a bylaw (City of Toronto, 2020b).

Research indicates that lawn watering can account for up to 90% of household water usage in urban areas (Survis and Root, 2016). Watering during peak daytime hours not only wastes water but also increases the risk of grass diseases due to evaporation (Survis and Root, 2016). With water demand expected to rise by 40% by 2050 and water shortages affecting more than half of the world's population by 2025, addressing this issue is crucial.

I strongly recommend that you introduce an enforceable bylaw to prohibit grass watering between 8 a.m. and 11 p.m. To ensure effective enforcement, the city should consider hiring additional bylaw officers to monitor compliance and address any violations. Voluntary changes alone are not sufficient, and given the urgency of the situation, we need to implement policies that compel residents to practice responsible water usage.
